newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian soldiers held over double murder.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian soldiers held over double murder.

text.p: Russian police on Saturday detained two army deserters suspected of killing the parents-in-law of a doctor who treats President Boris Yeltsin.

The soldiers' detention appeared to be the latest blow to the reputation of the demoralised and underfunded armed forces. Security forces were also hunting two soldiers following the murder of four of their comrades in Russia's far east.

Interfax and Itar-Tass news agencies quoted a police spokesman as saying two soldiers had been found in the northwestern region of Karelia with documents and other goods belonging to Andrei and Anna Ichko.
ORT television, which is partly own by the government, identified the Ichkos as the parents-in-law of Vladlen Vtorushin, who has been treating Yeltsin for two years.
Andrei Ichko was found dead with a skull fracture on Wednesday in the stairwell of the Moscow apartment block where his wife had been stabbed to death the previous day.
The motive for the attack is not known although investigators have said it appeared not to be political.
Yeltsin, 65, is in a sanatorium outside Moscow waiting to have a heart operation, probably in the next two months.
On the far eastern island of Sakhalin, army troops and elite police were still searching for two soldiers after four of their colleagues in an air defence unit were shot dead on Thursday.
Tass said one of the men had suddenly opened fire, killing a warrant officer and three soldiers, and both had then fled.
The shooting overshadowed an intended morale boosting tour of the far east by Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, but the minister said on Saturday he was generally pleased with his visit.

"On the whole I am satisfied with the state of affairs in the far east. The morale in the (military) district, the navy and the region is normal, making it possible for difficulties to be overcome," Tass quoted him as saying.
"The far eastern troops need only to be given some assistance. I think this assistance will be offered after I make my report to the government and the Russian president."

The far east, including the port of Vladivostok which is home to the Pacific fleet, has been particularly badly hit by financial problems besetting the armed forces as well as other sectors of the economy.
Yeltsin has expressed concern at the state of the armed forces and security chief Alexander Lebed has said they could soon mutiny.
Rodionov has ruled out a mutiny. He hopes the government will revise its draft budget for 1997, rejected at the first reading on Friday, to increase defence spending.
